macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Treasury doubles long-dated bond buybacks, easing pressure on yields
items.summary: U.S. Treasury announced it will increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds, a move that helped push bond yields lower and improved risk appetite across global markets. The policy shift was widely cited as the main macro catalyst behind the rebound in equities and gold.

items.title: Asian stocks surge as global bond markets stabilize
items.summary: Asian equities rose sharply, with South Korea’s KOSPI and Japan’s Nikkei leading gains after the Treasury buyback announcement reduced pressure in bond markets. Market reports also said U.S. futures were pointing to a firmer open in India, reflecting stronger regional sentiment.

items.title: Wall Street rebounds on lower Treasury yields
items.summary: U.S. stocks finished higher, with the S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq all posting modest gains as Treasury yields fell from multi-decade highs. The move was driven by expectations that increased buybacks would help lower borrowing costs.

items.title: Fed minutes showed divided officials and renewed rate-hike concerns
items.summary: Recent Federal Reserve minutes indicated growing support among officials for rate hikes, reflecting continued disagreement over the inflation outlook. Separate reporting said July U.S. consumer prices rose slightly, adding to the policy uncertainty.

items.title: RBI minutes turn hawkish, weighing on Indian bonds
items.summary: Indian bond markets sold off after RBI minutes signaled increased concern about inflation and suggested a possible rate hike if price pressures persist. Reports also said the rupee strengthened in early trade as U.S. Treasury buybacks eased dollar pressure.
items.source: The Economic Times / The Hindu BusinessLine

items.title: Global bond and currency markets react to Treasury move
items.summary: The dollar weakened broadly after the Treasury announced expanded buybacks, while the euro, pound, and yen all strengthened. Yields on longer-dated U.S. bonds also fell sharply from recent highs.

items.title: Semiconductor shares help lift Asia-Pacific equities
items.summary: A renewed rally in semiconductor stocks added to the regional market bounce, boosting South Korea’s KOSPI and Japan’s Nikkei. The move extended optimism already sparked by the Treasury bond-buyback announcement.

items.title: China and Australia renew currency swap agreement
items.summary: The People’s Bank of China and the Reserve Bank of Australia renewed their bilateral local-currency swap line and expanded it to 220 billion yuan, or A$46 billion, for five years. The agreement is intended to deepen financial cooperation and support trade and investment.

items.title: SMIC reports strong second-quarter profit growth
items.summary: Chinese chipmaker SMIC reported a 261.7% jump in second-quarter net profit, with revenue exceeding $3 billion. The result stood out as one of the major company-specific earnings developments in the region.

items.title: HDFC Bank plans $1 billion overseas debt raise
items.summary: HDFC Bank said it plans to raise $1 billion in overseas debt through bonds, taking advantage of a closing central bank FX swap window. The announcement adds a notable company financing development to the day’s market news.

items.title: Brent crude extends gains amid Iran tensions
items.summary: Oil prices continued rising for a fifth day after comments from U.S. President Donald Trump raised tensions with Iran. Higher crude prices added another macro pressure point for inflation-sensitive markets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin surges near $70,000, triggering massive short liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin jumped roughly 7%–8% in 24 hours and briefly touched the $70,000 level, its highest since early June, as a sharp short squeeze wiped out billions in bearish bets. Several reports tie the move to improved policy sentiment and macro liquidity developments in the U.S.

items.title: Ethereum rallies more than 17% as crypto market broadens its rebound
items.summary: Ethereum climbed about 17%–20% in the same period, pushing above $2,200 and at times above $2,300, alongside gains in XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin. On-chain tracking sources said liquidations on Ethereum alone exceeded $1.1 billion during the move.

items.title: Crypto market sees nearly $3 billion in liquidations amid sharp rebound
items.summary: Market data cited in several reports showed roughly $2.98 billion to $3.0 billion in crypto liquidations over the past 24 hours, with short positions making up the bulk of the losses. The liquidation wave helped amplify the price surge across major tokens.

items.title: U.S. policy developments fuel crypto rally, including SEC and CLARITY Act momentum
items.summary: Reports say the rally was supported by new U.S. regulatory and legislative developments, including SEC crypto asset rule proposals and renewed attention on the CLARITY Act. Coverage also noted meetings between crypto executives and U.S. officials focused on tokenization and the bill’s progress.

items.title: Treasury buyback expansion adds liquidity backdrop for crypto markets
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury’s decision to at least double long-dated bond buybacks was cited as a macro catalyst that improved liquidity conditions and supported risk assets. Market commentary linked the move to the day’s broader crypto rebound.

items.title: HSBC and Standard Chartered linked to tokenized deposit developments
items.summary: crypto.news highlighted a notable institutional blockchain development involving tokenized deposits tied to HSBC and Standard Chartered. The story points to continued bank adoption of blockchain-based settlement and deposit infrastructure.

items.title: CFTC seeks comments on AI compute derivatives
items.summary: The CFTC opened a comment process on AI compute derivatives, adding a new regulatory signal at the intersection of digital assets, AI infrastructure, and financial markets. The item reflects continued U.S. attention on novel financial products and market structure.

items.title: Ethena and FalconX launch $1 billion USDe lending facility
items.summary: A major project-development headline from crypto.news reported that Ethena and FalconX are launching a $1 billion USDe lending facility. The move expands institutional access to stablecoin-backed credit and signals ongoing growth in onchain finance.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI adds new privacy protections and teen-focused safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI announced new customer privacy measures and launched ChatGPT for Teens with parental controls, quiet hours, study tools, and stronger age-appropriate safeguards. The moves signal a broader push to balance rapid product expansion with safety and trust concerns.

items.title: Google expands Gemini with deeper research and browser integrations
items.summary: Google gave Gemini Live a Deep Research upgrade and widened Gemini in Chrome to more users, including Android users in the U.S. These updates indicate Google is continuing to embed Gemini more deeply into consumer workflows.

items.title: Amazon makes Alexa+ free on Fire TV
items.summary: Amazon removed the Prime requirement for Alexa+ on Fire TV, making its AI-powered assistant more widely available. The change suggests Amazon is using distribution and bundling to accelerate adoption.

items.title: OpenAI pauses frontier reinforcement learning work amid safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly paused some frontier reinforcement learning efforts as rapid model progress intensified safety and alignment concerns. The report adds to signs that leading AI labs are reassessing how quickly to scale training runs.

items.title: Murf AI launches Falcon 2 text-to-speech model
items.summary: Murf AI introduced Falcon 2, a new text-to-speech model designed for more human-like voices at lower cost and faster speed. The release adds to a wave of specialized AI model launches in audio generation.

items.title: OpenAI releases new security measures after Hugging Face hack
items.summary: OpenAI outlined additional AI security measures following a reported Hugging Face-related incident. The announcement underscores continued industry focus on model security and misuse prevention.

items.title: DeepMind weather model improves hurricane forecasting
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that DeepMind’s WeatherNext model is surprising weather scientists with more accurate predictions using lower-resolution weather data. The development highlights growing interest in AI for scientific forecasting.

items.title: Cloudflare gives AI agents an identity and wallet
items.summary: Cloudflare announced infrastructure intended to give AI agents identity and payment capabilities. The move reflects a broader trend toward building the plumbing for autonomous AI systems.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with stronger safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI’s teen-focused ChatGPT rollout adds parental controls and educational features aimed at younger users. It is one of the clearest product examples of AI companies responding to safety pressure.

items.title: Grok 4.6 and other new model releases accelerate August’s AI launch cycle
items.summary: Multiple new models reportedly arrived in quick succession this month, including Grok 4.6, Meta’s Muse Spark 1.2, ByteDance’s Seed 2.1 Turbo, and Z.AI’s GLM-5.3. The pace suggests model release cycles are continuing to compress across major labs.

items.title: India’s AI ecosystem faces talent and data bottlenecks
items.summary: A new study found talent shortages and poor data standardization remain major constraints on India’s AI ecosystem, even as open-source tool use stays high. The report points to infrastructure alone not being enough to drive AI adoption at scale.

items.title: China’s AI infrastructure buildout continues
items.summary: Reports say China is rapidly expanding data center capacity to support AI demand over the next five years. The trend reinforces how AI competition is increasingly tied to compute infrastructure and power availability.
